# F1TV-DL-WebUI: agent-assisted setup and support

> Help the user save supported F1 TV replays at home, then save complete MP4s to
> a travel device for offline viewing on planes, trains or slow connections.
> Success means durable storage and a verified local offline file, not merely a
> container that started. Read AGENTS.md as well. Keep this repository private.

## Current sources of truth

- [README.md](README.md): purpose, beginner Compose setup and offline workflow.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repository/security rules.
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml): effective mount, port and image defaults.
- [.env.example](.env.example): non-secret configuration examples.
- [Storage](DOCS/storage.md): persistence, capacity, permissions, mounted shares and NFS.
- [Operations](DOCS/operations.md): safe checks, backups, keys, updates and recovery.
- [Deployment](DOCS/deployment.md): Dockerfile, registry images and optional Drone.
- [Scripts](scripts/README.md): what runs automatically and which operation is destructive.
- [Home deployment](DOCS/home-deployment.md): existing maintainer infrastructure; do not apply its private host values to another user's installation.
- [License scope](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): original code is MIT; dependencies and content keep their own terms.

Historical implementation specs and dated plans are background, not current setup
instructions. Current user instructions take precedence. Do not change repo
visibility, publish images, reset a library or send credentials anywhere as an
implied part of helping someone install this app.

## Before building or starting anything

1. Determine whether this is a new installation or an existing library. Identify
   the actual Docker daemon/context, target host, OS and Docker Desktop VM if any.
   Host paths refer to the Docker server, not necessarily the agent's laptop.
2. Inspect existing state read-only. Preserve any current project/container
   identity, data bind/volume, external encryption key, media volume/options,
   required filesystem/marker, image, port and library. Never replace an existing
   configuration with generic defaults just to make startup pass.
3. Resolve Compose privately and report only relevant non-secret mount/type/path,
   port and filesystem settings. Prefer `docker compose config --quiet` for syntax
   checks. A full resolved config or `docker inspect .Config.Env` can expose a key;
   never echo it. Mount driver options can also contain credentials: redact them.
4. Check persistence for BOTH `/app/data` and `/app/downloads`. Check capacity on
   Docker's build/image filesystem, the actual media filesystem and eventually
   the travel device. If a check is unavailable, say so rather than guessing.
5. Verify the chosen physical/network disk is actually present and the intended
   source is writable by container UID/GID 1000. Validate network identity before
   creating folders or starting a download. Then choose the simple documented
   Compose path, with optional `DOWNLOAD_PATH`; Drone is not a prerequisite.

Do not install host Node/npm/FFmpeg for the Docker workflow. Docker supplies them.
Do not queue a real replay before storage checks pass and the user has requested
that download. Let the user enter F1 TV credentials privately in Settings.

## Persistence decisions and confirmation

- Default Compose `data` and `media` named volumes ARE persistent storage. They
  survive container replacement and ordinary `docker compose down`. Explain
  where Docker stores them and its capacity limits; do not falsely call them
  volatile merely because the user has no external disk or NAS.
- An explicit local/USB bind path can be persistent. Confirm the drive is mounted,
  the path is correct, parent directories are traversable and Docker Desktop has
  host-path sharing permission if applicable.
- If either application directory is only in the container writable layer, tmpfs,
  `/tmp`, or a disposable workspace, pause before using real credentials or making
  a library. Recommend persistent mounts. An intentionally disposable test needs
  explicit user confirmation; routine persistent installation does not.

Example: “This command has no persistent mount for your downloads/account data.
They would be lost when the container is removed or replaced. I recommend the
Compose file's persistent volumes. Is this meant to be a disposable test?”

- Named volumes are not backups. Never run `down -v`, remove/prune volumes,
  reset Docker Desktop, regenerate an existing key, or run the library-reset
  script as a normal installation or repair step. Do not delete user files to
  recover capacity without an explicit, specific deletion request.

## Capacity decisions

Use actual free bytes on the intended filesystem and any relevant VM/quota. A
directory's existence or total advertised drive size is not a capacity check.
A large NAS does not fix a full Docker build disk. A Mac/Windows host can have
ample free space while Docker Desktop's VM/disk-image allocation is full.

- Planning recommendations: 10 GB free for Docker builds/images, at least 1 GB
  allowance for local account/session data plus backups, and 20 GB free as a
  starting media budget. These are recommendations, not measured hardware minima.
  Add allowances when images, data and media share a disk/VM; do not count the
  same free bytes twice (about 31 GB total for those default starting allowances).
- Observed native 720p replays were 1.86–4.10 GB, not a guaranteed size range.
  Budget roughly 8 GB per long replay, all retained/queued files, working
  headroom for the largest planned replay again, and OS reserve. Ask how many
  replays the user intends to retain when that affects the disk choice.
- The runtime admission floor defaults to 2,000,000,000 bytes free. It is NOT a
  space reservation, per-job size estimator, full-queue capacity check or proof
  that a file will fit. Do not lower it to work around insufficient storage.
- If only 200 MB is available, stop before downloading: this is below the floor
  and far short of a normal replay. Offer an external drive, NAS, larger Docker
  disk/quota or user-approved cleanup. Do not proceed merely after a generic
  “are you sure?” if the planned replay cannot fit.
- Between the admission floor and the recommendation, explain the limited
  capacity and prepare a smaller explicit plan only if it actually fits with
  headroom. Unknown capacity is not a green light.

Example: “The selected download filesystem has only 200 MB free. The app needs
at least 2 GB before starting, and a complete race usually needs several GB.
Let's choose an external disk or mounted network share, or expand this storage.”

## Mounted and network storage

For an expected NAS, verify the actual server/share and filesystem on the Docker
host (`findmnt -T` on Linux or the platform equivalent). A plain directory at an
unmounted path can silently become local storage; Compose short binds can create
missing host directories. Do not create a substitute folder there or disable
checks to make the installation appear healthy.

If the expected share is absent, help restore it or explicitly choose another
real disk. Check NFS export authorization for the actual Docker client address.
Use narrowly scoped ownership/ACL fixes, not recursive changes to a whole share
or world-writable permissions. Keep SQLite and the provider session local.

In direct NFS mode preserve `REQUIRE_NFS=true`, the correct volume name/options,
`DOWNLOAD_MOUNT_OPTIONS=rw,nocopy`, and the matching `.f1tv-storage-id` marker.
Do not overwrite a marker to hide a wrong export. Named-volume options are fixed
at creation; changing them requires a migration plan, not volume deletion.
For SMB/CIFS or other host-mounted shares, verify identity at host level; the
application's NFS-specific guard does not validate every network filesystem.

## After startup, before claiming success

Use the non-secret mount inspection and bounded health command in
DOCS/operations.md. Confirm storage is `ready`, `writable` AND has sufficient
free bytes for the chosen plan; `ok: true` or a healthy container alone is not
enough. Do not spawn repeated blocked network probes. Fix an unavailable mount
or insufficient space before downloading rather than repeatedly retrying jobs.

Fresh installations automatically create a private persistent encryption key.
An existing external `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` takes precedence and must stay the same.
Never request, display, invent or commit real passwords, keys, cookies, session
files or signed media URLs. Preserve an existing key/data and diagnose failures
without resetting them. Backups contain sensitive state; protect them.

For an update, require idle work, take/verify a consistent backup, preserve mount
identity and verify the existing library afterward. The home Drone pipeline
aborts when queued/running work exists; it needs a retry once idle. Never cancel
the user's downloads simply to make a deployment pass.

## Offline-viewing acceptance

When the user requests a test, choose a supported replay they are entitled and
permitted to save, confirm actual queue progress AND file growth at the intended
storage, then verify completion and file delivery. A pre-2022 replay uses the
original main broadcast; 2022 onward requires F1 LIVE. All downloads require
native 1280×720, one English AAC track and full-duration MP4 validation. Unsupported
streams are errors, not permission to bypass DRM/regions or silently change feed,
resolution or language. There is no encoding service or segment-level resume.

The home-server copy is not the travel-device copy. Guide the user to Save MP4
on the phone/tablet/laptop they will take, wait for the complete file, verify
device capacity, and open/seek it locally with networking off. The web UI is not
an offline PWA. If the agent cannot inspect that device or playback, give the
user the remaining check and do not claim it was verified.

Offline intent and a subscription do not themselves establish copying rights.
Keep the README's personal travel framing, the applicable-terms note and license
scope. Do not present this as an official F1 TV/Netflix service, public replay
sharing platform or a guarantee of legal permission to archive content.
